semanticDecisions: the signals carry two bits per unit in 64: a dense alphabet sets almost every bit, and a mid-density one sets the bits of some units in most blocks, so a walk may pay a lookup through the canonical text per block, which costs more than the vectorized forward scan costs per block; eight lookups in at most sixteen walked blocks are the sign that the walk is paying

the judgement is per call and per unit: a unit the signals mostly reject keeps the walk (the walk then costs a signal read per block), a unit they mostly pass takes the lane; no field is added, so the invariant-6 lanes of the block structure are untouched
hits found through the exact masks inside the first blocks are unchanged; a hit after the hand-off is found by the graded windows from that point

measured and dropped: a run of consecutive non-rejecting blocks (two, eight or sixteen) fired on sparse text by chance or watered the dense gains down, and a count of saturated block signals (sixty of sixty-four bits) never fired on mid-density text, where the walk loses most

measured and kept out: the same hand-off in lastIndexOf lost (16384 dense ASCII units: 2,193 ns to 7,167, the flat String 6,177), because the stock reverse single-unit search is a scalar loop while the forward one is an intrinsic; a reverse lane built on the forward intrinsic is the next leaf
